title: Git: a history you can trust

questions.prompt: What is a branch in Git?
options: A copy of all the files
A name that points to one commit
A list of all commits by one person
questions.why: A branch is a movable name. When you commit, the name moves to the new commit.

wrong.0: Making a branch copies no files. That is why it is instant.
wrong.1: A branch is not a folder. All branches share the same working tree.
wrong.3: Commits by many people can be on one branch. Authors are stored in the commits.

questions.prompt: You delete the branch `houses` (never merged) with `git branch -D houses`. Its last commit is…
options: still stored, and `git reflog` shows its ID
questions.why: Deleting a branch deletes the name only. The commit stays for weeks, and the reflog knows it.

wrong.1: Git keeps commits without a name for weeks before it cleans them up.
wrong.2: Nothing moves to main unless you merge or cherry-pick it.
wrong.3: Git does not use the recycle bin. The commit is inside `.git`.

questions.prompt: A committed file contains `<<<<<<< HEAD`. What does that mean?
options: Git marks every merge like this for ever
The conflict was not resolved: the markers must go and the right text must be written
questions.why: Markers are Git's question to you. Committing them commits a broken file.

wrong.0: A resolved merge has no markers. They exist only until you write the answer.
wrong.2: Pushing shares the broken file with everyone.
wrong.3: Markers are plain text lines. They appear in text files.

questions.prompt: `.env` was committed last week. Today you add `.env` to `.gitignore` and commit. What is true now?
options: Git refuses to open the repository
Git still tracks `.env`, and the old value is still in history
questions.why: `.gitignore` only affects files Git does not track yet. History is not changed.

options: Reject marks above the stored maximum
questions.why: It says what changed and hints why, so a reader understands without opening the diff.

wrong.0: Fix what? The reader has to open every file to find out.
wrong.1: Which files, and why? Every commit updates files.

questions.prompt: `main` has not moved since `topic` was made from it. What does `git merge topic` on main do?
options: A fast-forward: `main` moves to `topic`'s commit, with no merge commit
questions.why: There is nothing to join, so Git moves the name forward.

wrong.0: Only with `--no-ff`, or when both branches moved.
wrong.2: A conflict needs changes on both sides. Main has none.
wrong.3: There is something to merge: the commits on `topic`.

questions.prompt: You have changes you never committed, and you run `git reset --hard`. What happens to them?
options: They are in the staging area
They move to a new branch
They are gone; nothing can bring back what was never committed
questions.why: The reflog lists commits. Uncommitted changes were never stored as a commit.

wrong.2: Git makes no branch for you.

questions.prompt: GPIS: a real key was pushed in a commit. What must happen first?
options: Change (rotate) the key, because anyone with the history has it
Delete the file in a new commit
questions.why: Copies of the history may already exist. Only a new key makes the old one useless.

wrong.1: The old commit still holds the key.
wrong.2: Anyone who already copied it keeps it.
wrong.3: Too late: `.gitignore` does not touch committed files.
